docs.text: Welcome to WhiskDB Docs This is the official project documentation for WhiskDB , an in-memory relational database and WebAssembly application host designed to execute application logic directly within the engine. Project Overview Traditional database architectures separate the database engine from the application tier with rigid network boundaries, incurring serialization, IPC, and round-trip network latency. WhiskDB eliminates this boundary by co-locating transactional business logic (sandboxed WebAssembly Whisks ) and relational state in the same physical memory space. Inspired by modern data systems such as SpacetimeDB , DuckDB , and Convex , WhiskDB delivers sub-millisecond in-memory execution combined with configurable Write-Ahead Log (WAL) durability, point-in-time snapshots, and real-time client reactivity. Academic Information This project is conducted as part of the Senior Capstone Graduation Project at OSTİM Technical University (Department of Software Engineering). docs.text: Developer Guide Welcome to the WhiskDB Developer Guide. This document defines the engineering standards, architecture, and collaboration workflow for all team members contributing to the project. External Libraries WhiskDB leverages external C++ libraries for low-level networking, protocols, storage, bytecode sandboxing, and configuration parsing: Library Component / Header Purpose Description Asio asio ( #include <asio.hpp> ) Asynchronous Network I/O Standalone, non-blocking asynchronous I/O and event loop framework driving WhiskDB's client/server TCP communication and framing. SQLite3 sqlite3 ( #include <sqlite3.h> ) Relational Storage & SQL Engine Embedded SQL engine compiled via C-amalgamation, responsible for B-tree index management, SQL dialect execution, and in-memory table structures. Wasmtime ( libwasmtime ) wasmtime ( #include <wasmtime.h> ) Sandboxed Bytecode Execution High-performance, memory-safe WebAssembly runtime executing user-defined Whisk functions in-engine with near-instant instantiation and resource metering. toml++ ( tomlplusplus ) tomlplusplus ( #include <toml++/toml.hpp> ) Configuration Parsing Header-only modern C++ library for loading, parsing, and validating TOML-based database configuration files ( config.toml ). Boost.Beast boost/beast ( #include <boost/beast.hpp> ) Networking & WebSocket Provides HTTP and WebSocket protocol implementations built on top of Boost.Asio . Powers WhiskDB's client connection handling, real-time reactive subscriptions, and network communication layer. Component Integration Details Asio : Standalone header-only integration ( ASIO_STANDALONE ) linked via asio_headers . Handles asynchronous socket read/write operations and connection lifecycle without runtime thread explosion. SQLite3 : Integrated as an amalgamation source build ( sqlite3.c ) compiled statically with -DSQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 -DSQLITE_OMIT_LOAD_EXTENSION=1 . Provides zero-copy in-memory execution and prepared statement caching. Wasmtime ( libwasmtime ) : Pre-compiles and caches .wasm modules to enable microsecond execution latency for server-side Whisks. Enforces strict memory sandboxing, gas/fuel limiting, and transactional savepoints during module invocations. toml++ ( tomlplusplus ) : Modern C++23 header-only TOML library ( toml_headers ) for reading engine options, network bindings, and durability modes. Boost.Beast : Managed via vcpkg ( vcpkg.json ) and linked in CMakeLists.txt via CMake's find_package(Boost REQUIRED) . Implements RFC 6455 WebSocket framing for real-time subscription streaming and binary message passing. Coding Standards & Conventions To maintain a clean and reliable codebase across the team, all contributors should follow these conventions: C++ Style Memory & Pointers Smart pointers only : Never use raw malloc , new , or delete . Use smart pointers for all dynamic allocations. Prefer std::unique_ptr : Default to std::unique_ptr for exclusive ownership. Use std::shared_ptr only when multiple owners truly need shared lifetime management. Types & Constants Fixed-width integers : Use explicit fixed-width integers ( int8_t , int16_t , int32_t , int64_t , uint8_t , uint16_t , uint32_t , uint64_t ) instead of standard types like int , long , or uint . Indices and offsets : Use idx_t instead of size_t for counts, offsets, and collection indices. Scoped enums ( enum class ) : Always use enum class rather than plain C-style enums. Explicitly specify the underlying storage type (e.g., : uint8_t ) only when the enum is serialized. No magic numbers : Name literal values using constexpr variables to provide clear meaning and context. Const & References Use const whenever possible : Mark variables, member functions, and parameters const by default if they should not be modified. Pass by reference : Favor references over raw pointers for function arguments. Const references for non-trivial types : Pass objects that are expensive to copy (e.g., std::vector , std::string ) as const & . Functions & Control Flow Return early : Keep nesting shallow and avoid deep if / else branches by returning early. Always use braces : Use curly braces {} for all if statements and loops, even for single-line bodies. Range-based loops : Prefer modern range-based for loops whenever iterating: cpp for (const auto& item : items) { // process item } Virtual overrides : When overriding a virtual method, omit the virtual keyword and explicitly use override or final . Namespaces No namespace imports : Never write using namespace std; or import entire namespaces into source or header files. Core namespace : All functions and classes under the core engine ( src/ ) must reside inside the database namespace. Class Layout Keep class structures consistent and easy to scan: 1. Public constructor(s) and public member variables. 2. Public member functions. 3. Private helper functions. 4. Private member variables. class MyClass { public: MyClass(); int my_public_variable; public: void MyFunction(); private: void MyPrivateFunction(); private: int my_private_variable; }; Naming Conventions Keep names clear and descriptive. Avoid single-letter variables except for standard loop counters in simple, non-nested loops. Target Convention Example Files Lowercase with underscores ( snake_case ) abstract_operator.cpp Types (classes, structs, enums, aliases) Capitalized words ( PascalCase ) BaseColumn , TupleBuffer Variables & Members Lowercase with underscores ( snake_case ) chunk_size , buffer_idx Functions & Methods Capitalized words ( PascalCase ) GetChunk() , ExecutePlan() Loop Indices Meaningful names in nested loops column_idx , row_idx ( i is only allowed in single loops) (Note: These naming guidelines are partially enforced automatically by clang-tidy .) Error Handling & Assertions Exceptions vs. Return Values Exceptions are for hard failures : Use exceptions only when an error terminates a query (such as SQL syntax errors, missing tables, or resource exhaustion). Return values for normal flow : If an error is an expected situation that normal execution can handle, return a status or result code instead of throwing. Test exception paths : Always write unit tests that trigger expected exceptions. If an error condition cannot be reproduced in a test, consider whether it should be an invariant assertion instead (rare cases like out-of-memory are exceptions). Assertions with D_ASSERT Catch developer bugs : Use D_ASSERT to verify internal assumptions and developer errors. Assertions should never be triggered by invalid user input. Assert generously with context : Add assertions whenever an assumption must hold, and always include a brief comment explaining the expected state: cpp // Validate that the target column index exists within bounds D_ASSERT(column_idx < column_count); AI Usage Policy AI coding assistants are helpful tools, but keep usage disciplined: - Take full ownership : Never submit AI-generated code that you do not fully understand and cannot explain or debug yourself. - Verify before submitting : Make sure any generated code adheres to our project conventions, passes tests, and doesn't introduce unwanted dependencies or formatting issues. Build & Test Macros Standard development operations can be executed with short unified macros: Macro Purpose cmake build-debug Configures & compiles in Debug mode ( build/debug/ ) cmake build-release Configures & compiles in Release mode ( build/release/ ) cmake run-tests Compiles Debug and executes all test suites with verbose failure reporting cmake run-tests <regex> Runs test suites matching the filter regex (e.g. cmake run-tests wal ) cmake bench Configures & builds Release and executes standard persistence benchmark cmake bench-compare [branch] Compares performance metrics against specified branch (default: master ) cmake clean Removes build directories All macros are implemented in scripts/macro.sh and can be extended by adding new command functions. Git & Collaboration Workflow Mandatory 5-Step Development Flow All contributors and AI agents must follow this explicit lifecycle for every task: Check & Update GitHub Issues : Inspect open issues: gh issue list and gh issue view <N> . Post an initial comment on the issue acknowledging work has started. Branch from dev : Sync dev : git checkout dev && git pull origin dev . Branch: git checkout -b feat/issue-<N>-<short-slug> . Build & Test with Macros : Run cmake build-debug and cmake run-tests . Ensure 0 compiler warnings and all tests pass cleanly. Conventional Commit & Push : feat(<scope>): <description> (Closes #<N>) . git push -u origin feat/issue-<N>-<short-slug> . Open Pull Request & Close Issues (MANDATORY) : Target branch is dev : gh pr create --base dev --head feat/issue-<N>-<short-slug> ... . Work is never considered finished until the Pull Request is opened and linked. Close or reference issues with Closes #<N> . Branching Strategy Branch Purpose main Production-ready, stable milestone releases. Protected. dev Active integration branch. All features merge here first. Commit Message Convention Keep commit messages concise and descriptive using the standard format: - feat(sql): add index scan operator (Closes #12) - fix(wal): handle torn page recovery in replay (Closes #17) - docs(dev): update developer guide conventions Pull Request (PR) Checklist Before submitting a PR for review, make sure: - [ ] Code follows our C++ style and naming conventions (passes clang-tidy ). - [ ] Code compiles warning-free via cmake build-debug . - [ ] All tests pass cleanly via cmake run-tests . - [ ] Assertions use D_ASSERT with explanatory comments. - [ ] PR targets dev and references Closes #<N> . - [ ] Any AI-assisted code has been fully reviewed, understood, and tested. docs.text: Project Development This page outlines the architectural foundation, durability strategies, and development macro workflows of WhiskDB. Architecture Overview WhiskDB eliminates traditional client-database network boundaries by co-locating server-side application logic and relational state within the same memory space. +---------------------------------------+ | Whisk CLI | | (whisk sql, repl, call) | +-------------------+-------------------+ | TCP Framing (Asio) +-------------------v-------------------+ | WhiskDB Core | | | | +---------------------------------+ | | | In-Memory SQLite Core | | | | (Relational Storage & Queries) | | | +----------------+----------------+ | | | Shared Memory | | +----------------v----------------+ | | | WASM Guest Runtime | | | | (Sandboxed Whisk Functions) | | | +----------------+----------------+ | | | | | +----------------v----------------+ | | | WAL & Storage Manager | | | | (Strict / Batched / Ephemeral) | | | +----------------+----------------+ | +-------------------|-------------------+ | +----------v----------+ | whiskdb.wal | | snapshot.whisk | +---------------------+ Key Subsystems Relational Query Engine : In-memory SQLite C-amalgamation core supporting ANSI SQL, indexed scans, and cached prepared statements. WASM Runtime Host : Embeds libwasmtime to execute user-defined procedural Whisks with transactional savepoint isolation, gas/fuel metering, and memory protection. Storage & Persistence : Configurable Write-Ahead Logging ( whiskdb.wal ) with binary framing, CRC32 checksums, and atomic crash recovery paired with binary snapshots ( snapshot.whisk ). Asynchronous Network Layer : High-performance, non-blocking TCP communication powered by standalone Asio and Boost.Beast . Durability Modes WhiskDB provides four durability levels to balance latency against persistence requirements. The mode can be configured in config.toml ( durability_mode ) or per-session: Durability Mode Config Aliases Disk Sync Strategy Crash Recovery Guarantee Primary Use Case MemoryOnly memory_only , ephemeral No disk I/O; purely in-memory execution. None. State is lost upon process termination. Unit testing ( whisk test ), staging sandboxes, and raw compute benchmarks. AsyncWal relaxed , async Appends WAL records to OS page cache without blocking on fdatasync . Survives process crashes. Risk of small data loss window on power failure or OS crash. High-frequency logging, telemetry, and sub-10µs write overhead workloads. SyncWalPerBatch (Default) group_commit , batched Appends to WAL ring buffer and periodically flushes via batched fdatasync . Zero data loss for all acknowledged batch flushes. Production workloads requiring optimal balance of SpacetimeDB-grade throughput and durability. SyncWalPerTx strict , sync Issues synchronous fdatasync before acknowledging each transaction. Complete durability against power failure, OS kernel panic, or hardware failure. Financial ledgers, mission-critical mutations, and strict compliance systems. Development Macros WhiskDB provides unified macro commands for standard development, compilation, and testing workflows. These commands can be executed directly using cmake <macro> or scripts/macro.sh <macro> : Macro Command Description Artifact Output cmake build-debug Configures and compiles the engine, apps, and test suites in Debug mode. build/debug/ cmake build-release Configures and compiles with maximum compiler optimizations in Release mode. build/release/ cmake run-tests Compiles Debug and executes all CTest suites with verbose diagnostic reporting on failure. build/debug/ cmake run-tests <regex> Runs only test suites matching the specified regex filter (e.g. cmake run-tests wal ). build/debug/ cmake bench Builds Release and executes the persistence and throughput benchmark suite ( whisk_bench ). build/release/ cmake bench-compare [branch] Runs the automated benchmark harness comparing current metrics against a target branch (defaults to master ). Benchmark summary cmake clean Removes all temporary build trees and cached dependency artifacts. build/debug , build/release Adding Custom Macros All macros are orchestrated through scripts/macro.sh . To implement a new development macro: Open scripts/macro.sh . Define a bash handler function: bash cmd_coverage() { cmd_build_debug echo "==> Generating code coverage report..." # Execute coverage tooling } Register the command pattern in the case "$SUBCOMMAND" in dispatcher block. External Libraries Summary WhiskDB integrates focused external libraries for networking, data storage, serialization, and sandboxed bytecode execution: Asio & Boost.Beast : Asynchronous networking, TCP session multiplexing, and WebSocket transport. SQLite3 : In-process SQL query compilation and relational table storage. libwasmtime : Fast, sandboxed WebAssembly execution environment. toml++ : Configuration parsing ( config.toml ). For deep architectural requirements, component links, and coding standards, refer to the Developer Guide .

User Guide WhiskDB provides a unified command-line tool, whisk , for interacting with the database engine, managing WebAssembly Whisk modules, executing SQL queries, and administering the database. Command-Line Interface (CLI) The whisk binary connects to a running WhiskDB server instance via TCP. Global Options These options apply across CLI commands and REPL sessions: Option Flag Format Default Description Host --host or --host= 127.0.0.1 WhiskDB server hostname or IPv4 address. Port --port

or --port=

8080 WhiskDB server listening port. Help -h , --help — Display CLI usage information and available commands. Command Reference The table below outlines all primary whisk commands: Command Usage Example Description whisk init whisk init my_service Scaffolds a new C++ Whisk module project with template source code ( whisk_guest.hpp ) and build scripts. whisk build whisk build Compiles C++ Whisk module sources into deterministic WebAssembly ( .wasm ) bytecode. whisk test whisk test Executes Whisks locally against an ephemeral in-memory ( :memory: ) WhiskDB instance before publishing. whisk publish whisk publish auth build/auth.wasm Deploys and hot-reloads .wasm bytecode modules onto the host database, running schema migration hooks. whisk call whisk call auth login '{"user":"alice"}' Invokes a registered Whisk function transactionally with optional JSON parameters. whisk sql whisk sql "SELECT id, name FROM users;" Executes a SQL statement over the connection and displays the result table. whisk logs whisk logs Retrieves structured in-memory execution and diagnostic logs from the server. whisk ping whisk ping Measures connection round-trip latency ( PONG in ). whisk snapshot whisk snapshot Triggers a manual snapshot checkpoint, flushing state to snapshot.whisk . whisk repl whisk or whisk repl Launches an interactive command and SQL REPL shell (default command when invoked without arguments). CLI Usage Examples Execute an ad-hoc SQL query: whisk --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 sql "SELECT id, username, email FROM accounts WHERE active = 1;" Check server connectivity and latency: whisk ping # Output: PONG in 312 us Fetch recent server diagnostic logs: whisk logs Interactive REPL Shell Starting whisk without arguments (or running whisk repl ) opens the interactive database shell: whisk> REPL Features Interactive SQL : Enter SQL queries terminated by ; . Multi-line input is supported automatically ( ...> prompt). Execution Timing : Each query displays execution duration in milliseconds along with formatted tabular output. Dot-Commands : Administrative and diagnostic commands prefixed with . execute immediately. Dot-Commands Reference Dot-Command Purpose Description .help Show Help Displays the list of available REPL dot-commands. .tables List Tables Queries and displays all user-defined relational tables in the active schema. .ping Ping Server Tests connection health and displays round-trip network time in microseconds. .logs View Logs Prints the latest server diagnostic logs directly into the terminal. .snapshot Trigger Snapshot Triggers a manual WAL checkpoint and persists an in-memory snapshot to disk. .quit , .exit Exit REPL Closes the client connection and exits the shell session. REPL Session Example $ whisk whisk> CREATE TABLE items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, price REAL); [OK] (round trip 0.85 ms) whisk> INSERT INTO items VALUES (1, 'Widget', 19.99), (2, 'Gadget', 49.50); [OK] 2 rows affected (round trip 1.20 ms) whisk> SELECT * FROM items; +----+--------+-------+ | id | name | price | +----+--------+-------+ | 1 | Widget | 19.99 | | 2 | Gadget | 49.50 | +----+--------+-------+ (round trip 0.94 ms) whisk> .ping PONG in 280 us whisk> .snapshot Snapshot created: 2 tables, 1420 bytes whisk> .quit Further Reading Project Development Overview Developer Guide & Architecture
